title: Sudbury impact
summary: An impact about 1.85 billion years ago produced the Sudbury structure in Ontario, Canada. Zircon ages from the impact melt are 1849.53 ± 0.21 and 1849.11 ± 0.19 million years. The original crater is described as at least 200 km across, a multi-ring basin of 200 to 250 km; the surviving igneous complex is an elliptical remnant about 60 by 30 km.

uncertainty.note: Zircon age 1849.53 ± 0.21 Ma (Davis 2008, as reported by Crater Explorer); a higher phase gives 1849.11 ± 0.19 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.

where.historical_name: Site of the future Sudbury Basin in what is now Ontario, Canada; no polities exist at this date

paleo.not_applicable: The MERDITH2021 plate model used by the project only reaches 1000 Ma; this event is about 1850 Ma.

importance.justification: One of the largest impact structures on Earth, whose melt sheet is dated to within a few hundred thousand years.

sources.title: Wikidata item Q281965 (Sudbury Basin), coordinate location (P625)

reviewer_note: Least sure of the original crater size: Crater Explorer lists 250 km as an estimate and 200 to 250 km elsewhere, NASA says at least 200 km. Crater Explorer coordinates (N 46°36′ W 81°11′) are given to the minute; pin uncertainty is half the stated diameter. Crater Explorer is a personal site, so the precise age rests on it alone; NASA gives only a rounded figure.
